component.intent: HTTP entrypoints for every Backend contract surface: public REST (sessions, messages, artifacts, cancel, close), public SSE (open / resume run streams), internal runner ingress (chunked NDJSON events, long-poll inbox), HMAC-authenticated webhooks, and ops health probes. Owns request parsing, dependency injection boilerplate, HTTP status mapping, and CORS. Owns no business rule of its own.
component.structure: One module per contract family, each contributing one `APIRouter` mounted from `src/main.py`: - sessions.py — public REST for Session lifecycle - stream.py — public SSE (POST + GET) - internal.py — backend←runner JSONL ingress (outbound only; the prior long-poll inbox endpoint `GET /internal/sessions/{id}/inbox` is gone — backend→runner traffic now flows over PGMQ) - webhooks.py — HMAC-verified runner webhook receiver - artifacts.py — presigned redirect for artifact bytes - stop.py — cancel-run forwarder - health.py — healthz / readyz Pydantic request/response models live alongside each router.

logic.rule: Validate path / body / query before any repo or registry call.
For state-changing endpoints, commit the DB transaction before returning the response so the caller's read-your-writes view holds.

For `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/messages` the user Message is appended and committed before the response is returned, so the caller can immediately open the stream and the runner sees the message in `prior_messages`.

For `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/stream` register the SSE subscriber on the EventBus BEFORE invoking the messaging producer (`cmp.backend.messaging.send_user_message`) so a warm runner's first frame is not dropped.

For `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/stream` the user-message enqueue is delegated to `cmp.backend.messaging`; the API module never calls `pgmq.*` or `NOTIFY` directly, never holds an `asyncio.Queue` of pending user messages, and never references `RegistryEntry.inbox` (which no longer exists).

For `POST /v1/webhooks/...` resolve the per-runner HMAC secret BEFORE running HMAC verification; reject with 401 if the registry has no entry and fallback is not allowed, never test the bootstrap secret against an unknown `runner_id`.
For artifact registration, audit row + ON CONFLICT INSERT + policy decision commit in the same transaction.

The persister coroutine `stream._persist_events` writes text deltas to `messages.content` AND tool-call lifecycle events (`TOOL_CALL_START` / `TOOL_CALL_ARGS` / `TOOL_CALL_END` / `TOOL_CALL_RESULT` / `CUSTOM ToolCallDenied`) to the `tool_calls` table, keyed by the AG-UI `parentMessageId` resolved through the lazy `_ensure_assistant_row` helper. Tool-call events without a resolvable parent are dropped with a logged warning.

component.intent: `ToolCallRepo` — the durable sink for AG-UI tool-call lifecycle events. One row per `(session_id, tool_call_id)`, linked by `parent_message_id` FK to the assistant Message the tool call belongs to. Re-emission across SSE drops is absorbed by `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (session_id, tool_call_id) DO UPDATE`. Re-emission of args concatenates server-side via `args = args || $delta`. State transitions are state-aware: a late `TOOL_CALL_END` does not overwrite a row already in `denied`. Result bodies are truncated at persistence time to `KLOC_TOOL_LIMITS.result_max_bytes` with a `…[truncated]` marker mirroring `runner/offload.py`.
component.structure: - `upsert_started(session_id, parent_message_id, tool_call_id, tool_name)` returns the row id; allocates `seq` via `(SELECT COALESCE(MAX(seq), 0) + 1 FROM tool_calls WHERE parent_message_id = ?)`. - `append_args_delta(session_id, tool_call_id, delta)` server-side concat; logs a warning and no-ops if the row is missing. - `mark_done(session_id, tool_call_id)` flips `state = 'done'` only when the prior `state = 'running'`. - `set_result(session_id, tool_call_id, result)` truncates and UPDATEs. - `mark_denied(session_id, tool_call_id, reason, hint)` flips `state = 'denied'`, sets reason / hint / `finalized_at`. - `list_for_messages(session_id, message_ids)` one-shot SELECT keyed by `parent_message_id IN (...)`, ordered by parent + seq.

component.intent: PGMQ-backed transport for backend-to-runner user messages. Owns the extension bootstrap, the per-Session queue lifecycle, and the producer-side `pgmq.send` + `NOTIFY` pairing that wakes the runner's `LISTEN` immediately. Queue identity is a pure function of `session_id` so it survives any `RegistryEntry` swap (warm-idle eviction, crash respawn, spawn-lock retry), structurally eliminating the queue-identity-drift class of bug documented in `tasks/fix-runner-inbox/root-cause.md`. Holds no `asyncio.Queue` of its own; the only stateful element here is the Postgres queue itself.
component.structure: - pgmq.py — `ensure_extension(conn)` (CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgmq), `inbox_queue_name(session_id) -> str` (`inbox_{session_id_no_dashes}`), `ensure_inbox_queue(conn, session_id)` (idempotent `pgmq.create_queue`), `send_user_message(conn, session_id, run_id, messages) -> msg_id` (pgmq.send + NOTIFY in one tx), `drop_inbox_queue(conn, session_id)` (called from Session.close).

logic.rule: Every `send_user_message` issues `pgmq.send` and `NOTIFY inbox_{slug}` in the same DB transaction so the LISTEN-ing runner cannot wake before the row is visible.
Queue identity is derived solely from `session_id` (`inbox_queue_name`); the function never reads any field of `RegistryEntry` or any other per-spawn object.
`ensure_inbox_queue` is idempotent — a second call with the same `session_id` is a no-op so producer-side callers never race on first-message creation.
`drop_inbox_queue` is called only from the Session-close path, never from runner eviction; pending messages must survive eviction.

component.intent: In-process pub/sub fabric that decouples AG-UI event producers (the JSONL ingress in `cmp.backend.api`) from consumers (the SSE generators in `cmp.backend.api` and the durable persister coroutine), plus a bounded replay ring so reconnecting Analysts can pick up from a cursor. Also owns the SSE encoder and the assistant-message text-delta debouncer.
component.structure: - event_bus.py — `EventBus` with `(session_id, run_id)` topics, register-before-publish API, essential vs bounded queues, slow-subscriber sentinel. - execution_registry.py — bounded deque (maxlen 10_000) per execution with monotonic `seq` + `replay_from(last_seq)`; evicts 5 min after terminal frame. - sse.py — `make_response` wraps an async iterator in a `StreamingResponse` and uses AG-UI's `EventEncoder`; stamps `id: <seq>` on each line. - agui_event_formatter.py — `normalize(event)` coerces Pydantic or dict to wire form; `is_run_lifecycle_terminal` for stream teardown. - debounce.py — `TextDeltaDebouncer` flushes a per-message buffer on 256 bytes or 250 ms to bound persister write QPS.

logic.rule: The persister registers with `essential=True` (unbounded queue) because dropping it would leave the DB with a prefix of the run.
SSE subscribers register with the default bounded queue; the slow-subscriber sentinel evicts them rather than OOMing the backend.

Seq is allocated exactly once per frame at the JSONL ingress boundary — `ExecutionRegistry.append` is the single source of seq truth so SSE and persister see the same number and reconnect cursors stay consistent.

component.intent: Per-Session runner lifecycle: spawn, heartbeat watch, warm idle, orphan sweep at boot, and inbox queue per Session. `DockerRunner` is the only concrete `Runner` impl and is the unit that talks to the Docker daemon. The registry is in-memory and process-local — single uvicorn worker.
component.structure: - protocol.py — `Runner` and `RunnerHandle` Protocols (spawn, terminate, is_alive). - docker_runner.py — `DockerRunner` + `DockerRunnerHandle`: create / start / stop(t=5) / wait / delete via aiodocker. Memory 1 GiB, 2 NanoCPUs, pids-limit 256, labelled `kloc.role=runner`. - registry.py — `RunnerRegistry` with per-session `RegistryEntry{handle, warm_idle, heartbeat, in_flight_tool_calls, ...}`, per-session spawn lock, in-flight tool-call tracking. The PGMQ migration moved the inbox out of the entry so there is no `inbox` field. - heartbeat.py — `HeartbeatWatcher` per-Session task; on timeout: terminate handle and fire on_crash callback. - warm_idle.py — `WarmIdleManager` cancels on user-message and evicts after the configured idle window. - sweeper.py — `orphan_sweep` at boot: kill any `kloc.role=runner` container the registry doesn't know. - hydrate.py — writes per-spawn `<runner_id>.json` into the hydration named volume and builds the aiodocker Mount dicts.

logic.rule: Spawn under the per-session lock so two concurrent stream calls cannot race two containers onto the same Session.

Heartbeat reset is driven by `type: "heartbeat"` / `RunnerHeartbeat` / `runner_ready` frames on the JSONL ingress; other AG-UI events do not reset the watcher. `runner_ready` is the runner's first emitted frame and counts as the cold-start beat.
On `RUN_FINISHED` start the warm-idle countdown; on the next user-message cancel it.
Boot orphan-sweep runs ONCE after the registry is wired and the registry is empty — every labelled container found is an orphan to terminate.
The hydration file is written before container `create` and is named with the spawn's `runner_id` so concurrent spawns cannot collide on a shared file name.
`get_or_spawn`, when reusing an existing entry, calls `warm_idle.on_user_message()` before `await_kill_in_flight()` so the countdown task is cancelled atomically as part of the reuse decision.

`WarmIdleManager.await_kill_in_flight()` blocks only during the terminate phase; during the countdown phase it returns immediately. Awaiting the countdown task here would self-block for the full warm-idle window.

component.intent: Thin async repositories that own all SQL the backend executes against `top.postgres`. One repo per aggregate plus the boot recovery sweep. Every method takes an `AsyncSession` injected by the caller — no module-level session, no implicit connection.
component.structure: - sessions.py — `SessionRepo` (create, get, close, touch_updated_at, set_runner_state, list_for_analyst). - messages.py — `MessageRepo` (`_next_seq` + `append` with savepoint+UNIQUE retry, `append_delta` server-side concat, `finalize`, `get`, `list_for_session`). - tool_calls.py — `ToolCallRepo` (`upsert_started` with `ON CONFLICT (session_id, tool_call_id) DO UPDATE`, `append_args_delta` server-side concat, `mark_done` / `mark_denied` state transitions, `set_result` with size-cap truncation via `KLOC_TOOL_LIMITS.result_max_bytes`, `list_for_messages` batched lookup keyed by `parent_message_id IN (...)`). - audit.py — `AuditRepo` (`append` validating against the locked 12-name vocabulary, `last_state_snapshot` via JSONB `@>` predicate, `list_for_session`). - artifacts.py — `ArtifactRepo.register` is `INSERT … ON CONFLICT (session_id, object_key) DO NOTHING RETURNING …` so duplicate webhooks from runner retries are absorbed without divergence. - boot.py — `sweep_orphaned_messages(conn)`: any Message with `finalized_at IS NULL` is finalized and a `stream_orphaned` audit row inserted.

logic.rule: Sequence allocation for Messages is `SELECT max(seq)+1` inside the same transaction as the INSERT, with the per-Session UNIQUE constraint as the atomic guarantee and a bounded retry on IntegrityError.
`AuditRepo.append` rejects any event_type not in the locked vocabulary so undocumented audit names cannot leak into the table.
`ArtifactRepo.register` is idempotent on `(session_id, object_key)` and returns `(row, created)` so the caller can audit every receive regardless of duplicate.

component.intent: SQLAlchemy 2.x async setup: the declarative base with stable alembic naming conventions, the async engine factory and sessionmaker, the FastAPI dependency that yields one `AsyncSession` per request, and the ORM table mappings plus the Pydantic `HydrationPayload` schema used to bind-mount runner bootstrap state.
component.structure: - base.py — `Base(DeclarativeBase, AsyncAttrs)` + `MetaData` with NAMING_CONVENTION. - engine.py — `create_async_engine` (pool 10, max-overflow 20, pre-ping) + `async_sessionmaker(expire_on_commit=False)` + module-level `get_engine` / `get_sessionmaker` accessors. - deps.py — `get_session` request-scoped generator. - models.py — `Session`, `Message`, `AuditLog`, `ArtifactMetadata` ORM tables + `HydrationPayload`, `McpStdioEndpoint`, `McpHttpEndpoint` Pydantic models + `AuditEventType` Literal of the 12 locked audit names.

component.intent: Webhook utilities: HMAC verification, policy decision, and an out-of-band audit-emit closure used by long-running coroutines (RunnerRegistry, WarmIdleManager, HeartbeatWatcher) that don't share the request-scoped session.
component.structure: - verify_hmac.py — `verify_hmac_signature` (HMAC-SHA256 over `f"{ts}.{body}"`, base64, 60 s replay window, constant-time compare); `sign_for_test` for tests. - policy.py — `Policy.decide` consults the deny-set fallback (`KLOC_DENY_TOOLS`) first, then a per-tool `ToolPolicyEvaluator` from `EVALUATORS` when the event is `BeforeToolCall`. Evaluator denials carry a `hint` field the runner threads into the `ToolCallDenied` AG-UI event. - stat_client.py — best-effort `stat(path)` against the kloc-intelligence `/v1/file_stat` endpoint; 500 ms single attempt; `None` on any failure (allow). - evaluators/__init__.py — `EVALUATORS` registry + `ToolPolicyEvaluator` Protocol. - evaluators/file_read.py — `FileReadEvaluator`. Denies whole-file reads larger than `KLOC_TOOL_LIMITS.file_read.max_bytes`; a byte-range read (`start_line`/`end_line`/`max_bytes`) bypasses the stat call. - evaluators/kloc_flows.py — `KlocFlowsEvaluator`. Denies unbounded `kloc_flows()` calls when `require_bounded=true`. - emit.py — `make_audit_emit_closure(sessionmaker)` returns an async `emit(event_type, payload)` that opens a fresh AsyncSession, writes one audit row, commits.

component.intent: Async S3 helpers — upload_bytes, presigned_get, and the canonical artifact object-key shape. Backend does not upload artifact bodies in production — that's the runner — but the helper exists for tests and small server-side writes.
component.structure: - s3.py — `upload_bytes`, `presigned_get(expires_in=900)`, `artifact_object_key(session_id, artifact_id, filename)`.

component.intent: Single typed `Settings(BaseSettings)` reading `.env` and the process environment. Pydantic validators enforce the LLM-provider key invariant at construction time so misconfig surfaces at boot, not inside the runner.
component.structure: One Pydantic settings class; `get_settings()` is `@lru_cache` so all callers see the same instance.

component.intent: Process composition root: the `lifespan` context that boots the engine, the S3 client, the RunnerRegistry + DockerRunner, runs the boot-time orphan sweeps, and registers every `APIRouter`. CORS middleware is installed BEFORE any router so preflight is handled by Starlette, not falling through to a 405.
component.structure: One `create_app()` plus the module-level `app = create_app()`. All injection wiring (engine, sessionmaker, S3 client, RunnerRegistry, audit-emit closure, EventBus singleton) is on `app.state` so downstream `Depends` can read it.

component.intent: Next.js app-router shell: the root layout, the landing page, and the conversation page. The conversation page is a server component that hydrates from the backend via `Promise.all` before passing data to the client conversation root.
component.structure: - layout.tsx — root layout, theme bootstrap inlined to prevent FOUC, fonts. - page.tsx — landing page; renders Shell + Sidebar + hero copy; does NOT fetch sessions server-side (Sidebar fetches itself on mount). - s/[sessionId]/page.tsx — async server component; `Promise.all([getSession, listMessages(limit=500)])`; on ApiError 404 → notFound(). - s/[sessionId]/ConversationClient.tsx — `"use client"` boundary that renders `<Conversation>` with the SSR-hydrated props.

logic.rule: Server-side fetches happen only on the conversation page; the landing page is fully client-driven.
SSR rendering must not open the SSE stream; the stream is opened by `useRunLoop` only when the Analyst submits a message.

component.intent: Same-origin SSE pass-through Route Handlers. Each handler validates the request, opens an upstream connection to `top.backend`, and pipes the upstream body straight back to the browser unchanged. No transformation, no inspection of the SSE payload, no buffering beyond what `fetch` already does.
component.structure: - route.ts — `POST /api/agent-proxy` forwards to `POST /v1/sessions/{thread_id}/stream`. - resume/route.ts — `GET /api/agent-proxy/resume` forwards to `GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/stream?run_id=&last_event_id=`. Both set `runtime = "nodejs"` and `dynamic = "force-dynamic"` so Next.js does not try to cache or pre-render them.

logic.rule: Validate `thread_id` (POST) or `session_id`+`run_id` (GET) before opening the upstream connection.
Preserve upstream status code; set Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform; Connection: keep-alive on the response.

component.intent: Typed HTTP client for the backend's public REST surface plus the AG-UI SSE consumer, the in-memory state reducer, and the `useRunLoop` hook that owns the stream lifecycle and reconnect logic. The client is the only place network requests are issued — components never call `fetch` directly.
component.structure: - api.ts — `listSessions`, `createSession`, `getSession`, `listMessages`, `closeSession`, `cancelRun`, `artifactDownloadUrl`; `ApiError`. - agui.ts — `openRunStream` (POSTs `/api/agent-proxy`) and `resumeRunStream` (GETs `/api/agent-proxy/resume`); SSE parser yielding `AGUIEvent`s. - reducer.ts — pure `applyAction(state, action)` covering every AG-UI event the runner emits plus optimistic / rollback / connection actions. - runLoop.ts — `useRunLoop` hook: opens the stream on submit, rolls back optimistic state on error, schedules exponential-backoff reconnects on disconnect, falls back to `listMessages` when the stream recovery window is exceeded. - types.ts — all wire shapes the frontend cares about: backend payloads + AG-UI events + view types. - theme.ts, time.ts, cn.ts — pure helpers, no I/O.

logic.rule: The browser uses `NEXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL`; the server uses `BACKEND_URL` — same module, branch on `typeof window`.
Every backend call goes through `jsonOrThrow` so non-2xx surfaces as `ApiError` with status + parsed body.
Streaming traffic goes through the BFF — never direct from the browser to `top.backend` — so the browser stays same-origin.

component.intent: Presentational React components for the conversation surface (Shell, Sidebar, Thread, AnalystBubble, AssistantBubble, PendingAssistantBubble, ToolCallCard, ArtifactChip, ConnectionBanner, ErrorBanner, EmptyState, InputBar, NewSessionButton, SessionListItem, ConversationHeader, ThemeToggle, BlinkingCaret, RailFooter, CodeChip). Each component reads view-model state and dispatches actions; none issues HTTP requests of its own.
component.structure: One `.tsx` file per component. Pure visual concerns — colors, layout, accessibility affordances. Stateful behaviour delegated to `useRunLoop` and the reducer.

logic.rule: The pending Assistant indicator is shown inside the conversation thread (carrying the Assistant's identity), not as a separate connection-status banner.
The Tool Denial style is visually distinct from a completed Tool Call in both colour AND label.

`AssistantBubble` renders `message.content` through `cmp.frontend.markdown-content` (a styled `react-markdown` tree), never as a raw text node inside a `

`. The user-side `AnalystBubble` stays plain text.

component.intent: Styled markdown renderer for assistant prose. Wraps `react-markdown` v9 + `remark-gfm`, supplies per-element component overrides themed with the existing Tailwind tokens (chip background for inline code and code blocks, accent colour for links), and constrains URLs through a whitelist `urlTransform` / `imageTransform`. Raw HTML in markdown source is NOT rendered — `rehype-raw` is deliberately not enabled, so `<script>` / `<iframe>` / other raw tags surface as escaped text. Used by `AssistantBubble`; not used by `AnalystBubble` (user messages are intentionally plain text).
component.structure: One `MarkdownContent({ content })` named export rendering `<ReactMarkdown remarkPlugins={[remarkGfm]} urlTransform={urlTransform} components={...}>` inside a wrapper `<div data-test="assistant-markdown">`. Component overrides cover `a`, `code`, `pre`, `p`, `ul`, `ol`, `h1`/`h2`/`h3`, `blockquote`, `table`/`th`/`td`, `hr`, `img`. Link `href` runs through `urlTransform`; image `src` runs through `imageTransform`. Inline-vs-block code is detected by the presence of a `language-*` className on the `code` element, because react-markdown v9 removed the `inline` prop.

logic.rule: `urlTransform` whitelists `http(s):`, `mailto:`, `tel:`, fragment (`#…`), root-relative (`/…`), and dot-relative (`./…`, `../…`) URLs; anything else (including `javascript:` and bare `data:`) collapses to `#`.
`imageTransform` whitelists `http(s):` and `data:image/`; anything else collapses to an empty string.
Every rendered link carries `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow"`.
No `rehype-raw` plugin and no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` anywhere — raw HTML in `content` is rendered as escaped text.
The blinking caret is rendered by `AssistantBubble` as a sibling element OUTSIDE the markdown tree, so half-typed tokens during streaming do not interact with the markdown parser at the DOM boundary.

component.intent: Container entrypoint: read the HydrationPayload, build the channel, the audit-hook sender, the MCP clients, the Strands agent, the AG-UI wrapper, then enter the long-poll inbox loop. Each inbound user-message triggers one `agui_agent.run(...)` pass; every yielded AG-UI event is forwarded via `channel.emit`.
component.structure: - __main__.py — `_run` lifecycle, `_run_one_turn` per inbound, first-turn-only merge of `prior_messages` with the inbound list to avoid duplication. - agent_factory.py — `build_agent` (Strands `Agent` with MCP tools + a set of subagents auto-discovered from `agents/<name>/AGENT.md` via `cmp.runner.agents-loader` + optional `file_read`), `_AuditHookProvider` that registers BeforeToolCallEvent / AfterToolCallEvent callbacks on the per-thread inner agent the AG-UI wrapper constructs. - model_factory.py — provider switch on `payload.llm_provider` (anthropic / gemini wired, openrouter / bedrock raise NotImplementedError). - mcp_clients.py — builds Strands `MCPClient`s from mixed `McpStdioEndpoint` / `McpHttpEndpoint` lists; HTTP path adapts the 3-tuple Streamable-HTTP client to the 2-tuple Strands expects.

logic.rule: The MCP `with` scope wraps the whole inbox loop — a client subprocess death is equivalent to a runner exit.
On the FIRST turn merge `prior_messages` with the inbound `messages`; on subsequent turns use the inbound list as-is (the backend already pushes the cumulative list).
On an exception inside `agui_agent.run` emit a synthetic `RUN_ERROR` frame with `cause: "runner_crashed"` so the backend's SSE consumers close cleanly and the warm-idle watcher fires.
The audit hooks must be registered via `StrandsAgent(hooks=[provider])` (not on the seed `Agent`) — the wrapper builds a fresh per-thread inner agent that does not inherit seed-agent hooks.

component.intent: Filesystem autoregistry that turns each `agents/<name>/AGENT.md` file on the runner-side `/agents` named-volume mount into a Strands `Agent` the orchestrator exposes as a tool (agents-as-tools). Replaces the formerly hardcoded sub-agent that the runner built at boot. Failure modes are quiet skips per file, never fatal: a single malformed pack must not take down the runner for every other session pointing at the same `/agents` volume.
component.structure: - `AgentSpec(BaseModel)` — frontmatter contract: `name` (`^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`, 1-64 chars), `description` (1-1024 chars), `system_prompt` (the markdown body, author-owned, no template prefix), `path`. - `discover_agents(agents_dir: Path) -> list[AgentSpec]` — walks `agents_dir/*/AGENT.md`, parses YAML frontmatter + body, returns the spec list sorted by `name`. Returns `[]` on a missing or non-directory path. - `build_subagents(specs, model, tools, reserved_names, audit_emit)` — for each spec, instantiates `Agent(model=..., name=spec.name, system_prompt=spec.system_prompt, tools=...)`. Skips specs whose `name` is in `reserved_names` (the MCP tool name set) and routes a `runner_subagent_load_failed` audit row via `audit_emit`.

logic.rule: `name` is unique across the directory; on duplicate, the first-by-sort wins and the second is skipped with a `agents.duplicate_name` warning.

On a `name` collision with an MCP tool, the subagent is skipped (MCP tool wins because renaming an MCP tool is not recoverable) AND a `runner_subagent_load_failed` audit row is emitted via `audit_emit`.
Malformed YAML / missing-required-field / invalid-`name`-regex is a quiet skip with a `agents.invalid_spec` warning; siblings keep loading.
Each constructed subagent receives the same toolset as the orchestrator: `[*mcp_tools, file_read]`. Per-subagent tool filtering is out of scope and tracked as an open item.
Each subagent inherits the orchestrator's `Model` instance. Per-subagent model override is out of scope and tracked as an open item.

component.intent: The single conduit to `top.backend`: outbound chunked NDJSON event stream, long-poll inbox iterator, and a 15 s heartbeat. Replays the in-flight attempt's frames on reconnect so terminal frames (RUN_FINISHED / RUN_ERROR) cannot be lost silently to a TCP drop.
component.structure: `BackendChannel` class with three async loops: `_stream_outbound` (single chunked POST whose body is a long-lived generator), `iter_inbound` (25 s GET long-poll), `_heartbeat_loop` (15 s `set_busy`-aware ping). The heartbeat loop emits the first beat at t≈0 — before the leading `asyncio.sleep` — so a slow MCP-init does not outrun the backend's heartbeat watcher. Outbound queue bounded at 1024 with a sentinel for clean shutdown.

logic.rule: On a transient transport failure (httpx.TransportError, response status 408, 5xx) prepend the whole attempt's frames to the cross-attempt buffer before draining the queue, so the next attempt's body iterator replays them in order — over-delivery is preferred to silent loss.

On a permanent rejection (response status in `PERMANENT_REJECT_STATUSES = {400, 413, 414, 415, 422}`) drop the offending frame, emit a single synthetic `RUN_ERROR` with `cause="frame_rejected"` and the upstream status, and continue draining; replaying a deterministically rejected frame loops forever.

The runner refuses to enqueue any JSONL line larger than `RUNNER_MAX_FRAME_BYTES`; oversized payloads are routed through the artifact-upload path and the AG-UI frame is rewritten to reference the returned `artifact_id`.
The inbox loop swallows `httpx.TimeoutException` and re-polls; other exceptions back off 1 s and continue, never propagate to the entrypoint.
The `shutdown` inbox frame ends `iter_inbound`; the entrypoint then exits the inbox loop and stops the channel cleanly.

component.intent: Strands hook callbacks that POST audit webhooks to the backend and translate backend responses into Strands cancellation semantics. Owns the HMAC signing, the 2 s BeforeToolCall deadline, the fire-and-forget AfterToolCall queue, the `ArtifactRegistered` path that also emits the AG-UI `ArtifactAttached` Custom event, and the per-run `_active_message_id` that links tool-call emissions to the assistant Message currently being streamed.
component.structure: - audit.py — `AuditHookSender.before_tool_call` (blocks ≤ 2 s, translates timeout/error/deny into `cancel_tool` plus a `CUSTOM ToolCallDenied` event, stamps `parent_message_id` on the webhook payload from `_active_message_id`); `after_tool_call` (fire-and-forget through a 256-slot queue, emits a `HookBackpressure` once on QueueFull); `register_artifact` (POSTs `ArtifactRegistered` then emits `ArtifactAttached`); `set_active_message_id(message_id)` setter driven by the AG-UI emitter wrapper in `cmp.runner.entrypoint` at TEXT_MESSAGE_START / TEXT_MESSAGE_END boundaries. - utils.py — `resolve_tool_call` unwraps the `skill_executor` wrapper so audit names surface the real underlying tool.

logic.rule: BeforeToolCall blocks until the backend responds OR the 2 s deadline; on timeout set `cancel_tool="policy_deadline_exceeded"` AND emit a `HookBackpressure` AND emit a `ToolCallDenied` for that toolCallId.
AfterToolCall is fire-and-forget through a bounded queue; on overflow emit `HookBackpressure` once but never drop BeforeToolCall.
`ArtifactRegistered` is HMAC-POSTed BEFORE the AG-UI `ArtifactAttached` custom event so the FE never renders a chip whose artifact_id has not yet reached the DB.
Stop drains the AfterToolCall queue under exclusive ownership AFTER cancelling the worker, so each in-flight POST is bounded by the per-request httpx timeout.

`_active_message_id` is updated only by the AG-UI emitter wrapper around `wrap_for_agui` and never read by callers other than the BeforeToolCall payload builder and the ToolCallDenied custom-event builder.

constraint.intent: API handlers reach the database only through a `*Repo` class; raw `select(...)`/`update(...)` calls are forbidden in `src/api/`.
constraint.rationale: Repositories are the single audit point for SQL invariants (sequence allocation, audit vocabulary check, ON CONFLICT semantics). Bypassing them in a route handler silently re-introduces ordering and idempotency bugs.

constraint.intent: API modules contain only request validation, DI, and HTTP status mapping. Business rules belong in domain code (repos / streaming / runner_mgmt).
State-changing endpoints commit the DB transaction before returning the response so the caller's read-your-writes view holds.
constraint.require: Every state-changing handler issues `await db.commit()` before its `return`.

constraint.intent: `src/streaming/` modules do not import from `src/db/` or `src/repos/`. The persister coroutine in `cmp.backend.api` is the boundary between the event bus and the DB.
Every per-execution buffer in `src/streaming/` is bounded: the EventBus subscriber queue is bounded by default, the ExecutionRegistry ring is a `deque(maxlen=10_000)`.
constraint.require: Subscriber queues are bounded unless `essential=True` is documented at the call site.
ExecutionRegistry rings are bounded `deque` with a `maxlen`.

constraint.intent: The only Docker client allowed in `src/runner_mgmt/` is `aiodocker`. No subprocess shelling out to `docker`, no docker-py.
`RunnerRegistry.get_or_spawn` acquires the per-Session spawn lock before any spawn-side effect (hydration write, container create).
constraint.require: All spawn-side-effects live inside an `async with self._spawn_locks[session_id]:` block.

constraint.intent: Every repository takes an `AsyncSession` by constructor or method argument; none constructs one internally.
constraint.require: Each `*Repo` exposes a constructor that takes one `AsyncSession` parameter.

constraint.intent: Repositories never call HTTP or external services; they do SQL only.
`AuditRepo.append` validates the supplied `event_type` against `AUDIT_EVENT_TYPES` and raises on miss.
constraint.require: `event_type` is checked against `AUDIT_EVENT_TYPES` at the entry of `append`.

constraint.intent: `tool_calls.parent_message_id` is `NOT NULL` and references `messages.id`. Persistence of a tool-call event without a resolvable parent message id is a no-op with a logged warning; the persister never invents a parent row from event-stream context.
constraint.require: The schema column `tool_calls.parent_message_id` is `NOT NULL` with a foreign key to `messages.id ON DELETE CASCADE`.
The persister branch for `TOOL_CALL_START` logs `persister.tool_call_start.no_parent` and skips persistence when `parentMessageId` is missing on the wire event.

constraint.intent: `src/db/` modules contain no HTTP, no boto, no httpx — only SQLAlchemy and Pydantic models.
The audit-event vocabulary is declared exactly once, as a `Literal[...]` in `src/db/models.py`, and is derived for runtime use via `get_args(AuditEventType)`.
constraint.require: `AuditEventType` is a `Literal` declared in `src/db/models.py` and re-exported only by importing it from that module.

constraint.intent: HMAC comparison uses a constant-time primitive (`hmac.compare_digest`).
constraint.require: `verify_hmac_signature` compares MACs with `hmac.compare_digest`.

constraint.intent: The out-of-band audit-emit closure opens a fresh `AsyncSession` per emit and commits before returning.
constraint.require: `make_audit_emit_closure` returns an async function that opens its own `AsyncSession` and commits.

constraint.intent: `Policy.decide` consults a per-tool `ToolPolicyEvaluator` registry when `event_type == BeforeToolCall`; the evaluator inspects `args` and may deny with a reason and a hint.
constraint.require: Per-tool evaluators are looked up in `EVALUATORS` by `tool_name`.
An evaluator deny response carries `reason` namespaced under `tool_limit:*` and an optional `hint` string.

constraint.intent: Stat-call failure returns `allow`; the cap is guidance, not a security boundary.
constraint.require: `stat_client.stat` returns `None` on any failure and the evaluator returns `None` (allow) when the stat is unavailable.

constraint.intent: `src/storage/` does not import the ORM; it deals only in S3 API calls.
Configuration values are read from `Settings` only. Application code never calls `os.environ` for kloc-agent config — settings.py is the single source.
`CORSMiddleware` is added before `include_router` calls so browser preflight is handled by Starlette and never falls through to a router's 405.
constraint.require: The `add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, ...)` call precedes every `include_router(...)` call in `create_app`.

constraint.intent: Lifespan boots dependencies in a fixed order: DB engine → S3 client → RunnerRegistry → orphan-container sweep → DB orphan-message scan. Misconfig (missing greenlet, import errors) is allowed to crash boot; only transient operational errors (DB unreachable) are caught.
constraint.require: Lifespan creates the engine, then the S3 client, then the registry, then runs `orphan_sweep`, then runs `sweep_orphaned_messages` — in that order.
Only `OperationalError | InterfaceError | DBAPIError` are caught around the boot orphan-message scan.

constraint.intent: Network requests (`fetch`, `EventSource`) live in `frontend/src/lib/` only — components never issue HTTP themselves.
Browser-initiated SSE traffic goes through `/api/agent-proxy*`, never directly to the backend host.
The BFF route handlers do not parse, transform, or inspect the SSE body; they pipe `upstream.body` straight back with the same content-type and minimal Cache-Control / Connection adjustments.
Components consume state via props and dispatch via callbacks; they do not import from `lib/api.ts` to issue a request inside a render path.
A Tool Denial is conveyed by both colour and label, never colour alone, and is visually distinct from a completed Tool Call.
constraint.require: The denied state of `ToolCallCard` renders both a denial label and a distinct colour treatment.

constraint.intent: `MarkdownContent` MUST NOT enable `rehype-raw` or any plugin that allows raw HTML in markdown source. Raw HTML in `message.content` is rendered as escaped text.

Links rendered by `MarkdownContent` open in a new tab (`target="_blank"`) with `rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow"`. The `href` is run through `urlTransform` which permits only `http(s):`, `mailto:`, `tel:`, fragment, root-relative, and dot-relative URLs.
constraint.require: The `a` component override sets `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow"` on every rendered anchor.
`urlTransform` is passed to `<ReactMarkdown>` and rewrites any non-whitelisted scheme to `#`.

constraint.intent: The MCP client context manager(s) wrap the entire inbox loop, so a subprocess death is equivalent to a runner exit.
constraint.require: `async with contextlib.AsyncExitStack() as stack:` enters every MCP client before the `async for inbound in channel.iter_inbound():` loop, and the loop runs INSIDE that `with` block.

constraint.intent: On the first turn of a warm container the runner prepends `payload.prior_messages` to `inbound.messages`; on subsequent turns it uses `inbound.messages` only.
constraint.require: The runner tracks a `first_turn` boolean that flips false after the first successful `_run_one_turn`.

constraint.intent: On a transient outbound failure (httpx.TransportError or response status 408 or 5xx) the channel prepends every frame yielded during the broken attempt back into the pending buffer BEFORE draining the queue, so the next attempt's body iterator replays them in original order. Over-delivery is preferred to silent loss of terminal frames; the AG-UI consumer tolerates duplicate intermediates.
constraint.require: `yielded_this_attempt` is prepended to `pending_after_break` on the transient-failure branch.

constraint.intent: On a permanent rejection (response status in `PERMANENT_REJECT_STATUSES = {400, 413, 414, 415, 422}`) the channel drops the offending frame, emits a single synthetic `RUN_ERROR` AG-UI event carrying `cause="frame_rejected"` and the upstream status, and continues draining the queue. Replaying a deterministically-rejected frame loops forever and starves the persister.
constraint.require: `PERMANENT_REJECT_STATUSES` is a single named `frozenset[int]` at module scope in `runner/channel.py`.
The offending frame is removed from the replay buffer before the next attempt.

constraint.intent: When `RunnerRegistry.get_or_spawn` finds a warm `RegistryEntry`, it calls `entry.warm_idle.on_user_message()` BEFORE `entry.warm_idle.await_kill_in_flight()`. Inverting that order causes the handler to self-block for the entire warm-idle window because the countdown task only completes when the activity event is set, which the caller cannot do until `get_or_spawn` returns.
constraint.require: `on_user_message()` precedes `await_kill_in_flight()` on the warm-entry-found branch.
`WarmIdleManager.await_kill_in_flight()` is a no-op while `_killing is False`.

constraint.intent: `runner/channel.py` does not import the LLM provider SDKs or call them — its only counterparty is `top.backend`.

The runner's `_heartbeat_loop` emits the first `type: heartbeat` frame BEFORE the first `asyncio.sleep(HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_S)`. The `runner_ready` frame is the de-facto first beat at the ingress level; the explicit `heartbeat` frame follows promptly.
constraint.require: `_heartbeat_loop` performs its first `emit` before the leading sleep.

constraint.intent: Subagent `name` (from `AGENT.md` frontmatter) must be unique across `agents/<*>/AGENT.md` and must not collide with any MCP tool name advertised at runner startup. Collisions are skipped with a `runner_subagent_load_failed` audit row; load does not abort.
constraint.require: `build_subagents` consults a `reserved_names: set[str]` of MCP tool names and skips any spec whose `name` is in the set.
On a duplicate `name` across two AGENT.md files the first by sort order wins; the second is skipped with a `agents.duplicate_name` warning.

constraint.intent: `AuditHookSender.before_tool_call` blocks at most 2 s on the backend round-trip; the httpx client is constructed with `timeout=HOOK_DEADLINE_S`.
constraint.require: `AuditHookSender._http = httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=HOOK_DEADLINE_S)`.

constraint.intent: `AfterToolCall` flows through a bounded asyncio queue (maxsize 256). On `QueueFull` the sender emits a single `HookBackpressure` CUSTOM event but never blocks the agent loop.
constraint.require: The After queue uses `put_nowait` and catches `asyncio.QueueFull`.

constraint.intent: `AuditHookSender._active_message_id` is set on MessageStartEvent (AG-UI TEXT_MESSAGE_START) and cleared on MessageStopEvent (AG-UI TEXT_MESSAGE_END). It MUST NOT outlive a run: any tool-call audit emission produced when no assistant message is open carries no `parent_message_id`, and the FE reducer drops such an event with a console warning rather than synthesising a parent.
constraint.require: `set_active_message_id(message_id)` is called by the AG-UI emitter wrapper on TEXT_MESSAGE_START.
`set_active_message_id(None)` is called by the AG-UI emitter wrapper on TEXT_MESSAGE_END.
